suggestions.reason: The existing clause omits two standard integration clause requirements that expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to material legal risk. First, without an express statement that this Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and communications on the same subject matter, a counterparty could invoke pre-contractual negotiations, letters of intent, or earlier arrangements to vary or supplement the Agreement's terms in ways unfavorable to Sunesis. Second, the absence of a fraud carve-out means that the integration clause could, in certain jurisdictions, be construed to bar Sunesis from pursuing claims grounded in fraudulent pre-contractual misrepresentations, eliminating a critical common-law remedy. Both omissions are standard, market-accepted elements of an integration clause and their absence creates avoidable litigation exposure for Sunesis.
suggestions.original_text: Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Integration; Precedence. This Agreement, together with any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, supersedes all prior agreements, representations, and communications relating to such subject matter, and nothing herein shall limit either party's liability for fraud. Any such Work Order, Change Order, or exhibit will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

suggestions.reason: The current definition of "Sponsor Confidential Information" contains no express statement that information is protected regardless of whether it is marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure, creating a material enforcement risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: Quintiles could argue that unlabeled or verbally disclosed data does not qualify, leaving critical proprietary research, clinical, and pricing information unprotected. Additionally, the paragraph imposes no express obligation on Quintiles to protect Sponsor Confidential Information to any defined standard of care, whereas the separate Quintiles confidentiality provision establishes its own proprietary rights, creating a structurally asymmetric arrangement that leaves Sunesis with a less enforceable position in the event of unauthorized use or disclosure. This gap is particularly acute given the sensitive pharmaceutical data Sunesis would disclose in the performance of Services under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter "Sponsor Confidential Information"), written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor, whether or not marked, labeled, or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure. Quintiles shall protect Sponsor Confidential Information using no less than the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information, and in no event less than reasonable care.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to three material gaps: it imposes no measurable standard of care on Quintiles when handling Sunesis's proprietary pharmaceutical and clinical data, meaning Quintiles could apply minimal or inconsistent internal protections without breaching this provision; the need-to-know restriction governs only inter-party disclosure and does not require that Quintiles's employees or subcontractors receiving Sunesis's Confidential Information be themselves bound by equivalent confidentiality obligations, leaving Sunesis's data commercially unprotected at the recipient level; and there is no obligation on Quintiles to return or destroy Sunesis's Confidential Information at the end of a Work Order or on demand, allowing indefinite retention of sensitive proprietary information. Given the nature of pharmaceutical development data, each of these deficiencies creates significant financial and competitive exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than reasonable care. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees and authorized contractors only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder, provided that such employees and authorized contractors are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. Upon written request by the disclosing party, or upon the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the disclosing party and, upon request, certify such destruction in writing to the disclosing party. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause vests ownership of Sponsor's Property in Sunesis Pharmaceuticals but entirely fails to define the scope on which Quintiles may use that property, leaving Quintiles free to argue an implied broad licence or, conversely, to claim it has no licence at all and cannot perform the Services—both outcomes harmful to Sunesis. The absence of any use restriction means Quintiles faces no contractual barrier to applying Sunesis's proprietary inventions, trade secrets, or know-how outside the scope of this Agreement, including for the benefit of competing sponsors. The clause also allocates no responsibility to Quintiles for third-party infringement claims arising from its use of Sponsor's Property, exposing Sunesis to unindemnified IP litigation risk. These gaps interact with the IP ownership provisions elsewhere in the Agreement and should be read alongside any surviving indemnification obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor hereby grants Quintiles a non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited licence to use Sponsor's Property solely to perform the Services under this Agreement, and Quintiles shall not use Sponsor's Property for any other purpose. Quintiles shall be responsible for, and shall indemnify Sponsor against, any third-party claims arising from Quintiles' unauthorized use of Sponsor's Property.

suggestions.reason: The clause defines Quintiles' Property by reference to IP "developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement," but it does not separately and explicitly categorize background IP (pre-existing) from foreground IP (created during performance of this Agreement). This ambiguity creates a material risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: Quintiles could assert that IP generated during the engagement, using Sunesis data or know-how, qualifies as "independent of this Agreement" on the basis that Quintiles' own methods and personnel drove the development—potentially extinguishing Sunesis's ownership claim over what should be Sponsor-derived IP. The carve-out at the end of the clause offers partial protection, but its scope is narrower than required, as it only captures IP that "incorporates data, information or know-how derived from" Sponsor's Property, leaving uncovered scenarios where Sunesis's Confidential Information was used as a development input without being formally incorporated. Strengthening the definitional boundary of "independent of this Agreement" and broadening the carve-out will protect Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's ownership interests and ensure proper alignment with Section 6.3a.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles' Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles prior to or independently of this Agreement and without use of Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information, which relates to Quintiles' business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively "Quintiles' Property"). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles' Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates, is derived from, or was developed using Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information, all of which shall be governed by Section 6.3a.

suggestions.reason: The clause assigns newly created Project IP to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals but fails to expressly confirm that each party's pre-existing intellectual property remains its own, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals exposed to an argument that background IP contributed to the Services is affected by the assignment mechanism. More critically, the clause is entirely silent on third-party infringement risk: if Quintiles incorporates its own proprietary tools, methods, or Quintiles' Property into the Services and that material infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals bears no contractual remedy and could face exposure as the ultimate owner of the resulting Project IP. These gaps leave Sunesis Pharmaceuticals without a clear indemnity shield precisely when Quintiles is the party selecting and deploying the potentially infringing materials.
suggestions.original_text: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively "Project IP") are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Each party retains sole and exclusive ownership of its intellectual property existing prior to or independently of this Agreement, and no rights in such pre-existing intellectual property are transferred by this Agreement except as expressly stated herein. Quintiles shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Sponsor against any third-party claim alleging that Quintiles' Property incorporated into the Services infringes such third party's intellectual property rights. Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

suggestions.reason: The license grant as drafted creates material operational risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals in two respects. First, the exclusion of Affiliates and authorized third parties means that Sunesis's subsidiary entities, development partners, or regulatory-facing contractors cannot lawfully use the Quintiles Software to access study data, which is commercially unworkable for a pharmaceutical company whose data review and regulatory submissions routinely involve Affiliates and specialist contractors. Second, the license contains no stated duration independent of the vague "no longer necessary" trigger, which Quintiles could interpret unilaterally to demand return of the software and thereby cut off Sunesis's access to its own study data before applicable regulatory retention periods have elapsed. These gaps materially undermine Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's ability to satisfy post-study regulatory and data-access obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs) is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license, for the duration of this Agreement and for so long as Sponsor or its Affiliates are required to retain or access the study data under applicable law or regulatory requirements, with the right to use by Sponsor and its Affiliates and authorized third-party contractors acting on Sponsor's behalf, solely for the purpose of accessing, retrieving, or using the study data generated in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement, and without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles' Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, as confirmed by mutual written agreement of the parties, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The current clause is framed solely as a negative restriction—neither party acquires implied rights in the other's intellectual property—but it does not affirmatively confirm that each party owns and retains its pre-existing intellectual property rights. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, this gap creates material risk: in the absence of an express retention clause, any intellectual property contributed by Sunesis to the engagement (including proprietary compounds, clinical data, or pharmaceutical know-how) lacks a clear ownership anchor within this Agreement, potentially inviting disputes about whether development activity under the Agreement affected Sunesis's underlying ownership. The addition of an affirmative pre-existing IP retention statement closes this gap and provides Sunesis with a defensible ownership baseline throughout the term and following termination.
suggestions.original_text: No Implied Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: No Implied Rights. Each party retains all right, title and interest in and to its own intellectual property rights existing prior to or developed independently of this Agreement. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to three material gaps: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation on Quintiles, no mutual obligation requiring either party to notify the other of a material compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no commitment by Quintiles to address forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking in its supply chain. Left unaddressed, these omissions could expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to regulatory liability and reputational harm if Quintiles engages in corrupt conduct or uses non-compliant supply-chain partners, with no contractual recourse and no early-warning mechanism to allow Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to mitigate a developing compliance failure. The absence of a breach notification obligation is particularly acute given the heavily regulated pharmaceutical development context in which the Services are performed.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and applicable laws and standards relating to forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance of this Agreement. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

suggestions.reason: The current provision grants Sponsor a unilateral termination-for-convenience right but is otherwise entirely silent on what happens after notice is given, creating material operational and financial risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. Without an express transition assistance obligation, Quintiles faces no contractual duty to return Sponsor data and materials, cooperate with a replacement provider, or continue supporting ongoing studies during wind-down, leaving Sunesis potentially unable to transfer critical clinical work without interruption. The absence of any survival clause means that obligations fundamental to Sunesis's interests—including confidentiality, intellectual property ownership, indemnification, and payment—are not expressly preserved beyond termination, creating enforceability uncertainty. These gaps collectively expose Sunesis to both operational disruption and legal vulnerability at the precise moment it exercises its termination right.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Quintiles. Upon any termination, Quintiles shall promptly return all Sponsor data and materials in an agreed format and, at Sponsor's request, provide reasonable transition assistance—including cooperation with any successor provider—for up to ninety (90) days at then-current rates. Provisions relating to confidentiality, intellectual property, indemnification, and payment obligations shall survive termination.

suggestions.reason: The clause requires only a "close-out schedule" upon expiry of the cure period, with no obligation on Quintiles to prepare or execute a transition plan transferring ongoing work, data, regulatory submissions, or operational responsibilities to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals or its designee. For a pharmaceutical master services agreement, where Services may encompass active clinical trials, regulatory filings, or safety monitoring, the absence of a formal transition obligation creates a material operational risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: Quintiles could cease performance without an orderly handover, potentially jeopardizing regulatory timelines or patient safety obligations. This gap leaves Sunesis Pharmaceuticals without an enforceable mechanism to compel Quintiles to cooperate in migrating work to a replacement service provider, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to program delays and increased costs. The survival and consequences-of-termination provisions should be reviewed to confirm that transition assistance obligations survive expiry or termination of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule and transition plan, which shall address the orderly transfer of work, data, materials, and regulatory submissions to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals or its designee, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out or transition of the Services or required by laws or regulations. Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days following termination, at Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' reasonable direction and expense.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits Quintiles to discharge its obligations through corporate affiliates without expressly preserving Quintiles' primary liability to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, meaning that if an affiliate underperforms, Sunesis may find its direct contractual remedy against Quintiles impaired in practice. Additionally, the definition of "control" contains a typographical error ("polices" instead of "policies") and extends to any entity where a party merely has the undefined "ability to influence and direct" the policies and direction of an entity — a standard that is materially broader and more subjective than the fifty percent (50%) voting-securities threshold and could expose Sunesis to obligations toward, or bind Work Orders with, entities that Quintiles does not conventionally control. These combined deficiencies — undiluted affiliate delegation without retained primary responsibility, and an indeterminate affiliate universe — create material operational and financial risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order; provided that Quintiles shall remain primarily liable to Sponsor for the performance of any such affiliate as if Quintiles had performed such obligations directly. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor's affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor's affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term "affiliate" shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term "control" shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the contractual or legal right to direct the management, policies, and direction of an entity.

suggestions.reason: The exculpatory provision is entirely one-sided: it shields Quintiles from liability for errors, delays, or other consequences arising from Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' alleged failure to cooperate, while imposing no corresponding protection on Sunesis when Quintiles fails to provide information, materials, or cooperation that Sunesis may need. The undefined phrase "or to otherwise cooperate" is dangerously broad, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to arguments that virtually any performance failure by Quintiles is excused on the basis of some alleged cooperative shortcoming, without any objective standard for what cooperation requires. Additionally, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' obligation to forward documents "in a timely manner" is an undefined standard that creates a low-threshold trigger for Quintiles to invoke its exculpation, while Quintiles' own delivery obligation is qualified by the more protective "commercially reasonable efforts" standard. These asymmetries collectively create material financial and legal exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals under any disputed Work Order.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles within a commercially reasonable time all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services, and Quintiles shall provide Sponsor with all documents, materials and information in Quintiles' possession or control reasonably necessary for Sponsor to exercise its rights under this Agreement or the relevant Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Neither party shall be liable to the other nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising solely from the other party's failure to timely provide documents, materials or information as required under this Section or the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause imposes an absolute obligation on Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to disclose "all information available to it" regarding hazards and to "comply with all current legislation and regulations" concerning shipment, with no materiality threshold or reasonableness qualifier on either obligation. The absence of a "reasonably available" standard on the disclosure obligation, and the absence of an "in all material respects" or "applicable" qualifier on the compliance obligation, means that any technical gap in disclosure or any minor, immaterial regulatory non-conformity could constitute a breach and expose Sunesis to uncapped financial liability under the Agreement's indemnification and breach remedies provisions. This creates disproportionate and open-ended exposure for Sunesis where the trigger for liability is not tied to fault, knowledge, or materiality.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information reasonably available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply in all material respects with all applicable legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

suggestions.reason: The WORK ORDER section contains no operative text, leaving a critical gap in the Agreement: without an express order-of-precedence rule, any conflicting term in a Work Order could be argued to override the Master Services Agreement, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to the risk that project-level documents—potentially drafted or proposed by the counterparty—silently displace negotiated MSA protections such as liability caps, indemnification obligations, and confidentiality terms. Additionally, the absence of a battle-of-the-forms exclusion means that pre-printed or online terms attached to or referenced in a Work Order could be treated as incorporated into the Agreement, creating further uncontrolled exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. These gaps should be read alongside the Agreement's limitation of liability and indemnification provisions, as any precedence ambiguity could undermine those protections.
suggestions.original_text: WORK ORDER
suggestions.suggested_fix:
WORK ORDER

Each Work Order is incorporated into and governed by this Agreement. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between a Work Order and this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall govern and control, except to the extent the Work Order expressly states, with specific reference to the conflicting provision, that it supersedes a specified term of this Agreement. No pre-printed, standard, or online terms attached to or referenced in any Work Order shall form part of this Agreement or bind either party.

suggestions.reason: The opening sentence references the Master Agreement but fails to identify all documents that collectively govern the Work Order, such as attachments and exhibits to the Work Order itself, leaving the full contractual framework incomplete and legally uncertain. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, this gap creates a material risk that Quintiles could dispute whether specific scope documents, budget schedules, or technical exhibits are binding, undermining Sunesis's ability to hold Quintiles to agreed deliverables and costs. Without a completeness statement identifying all constituent documents, the boundary of Quintiles's obligations is undefined, exposing Sunesis to scope and pricing disputes that have no clear contractual anchor. This provision should also be read alongside any order-of-precedence mechanism in the Master Agreement to confirm which document controls in the event of conflict.
suggestions.original_text: This Work Order (“Work Order”) is between ________ (“Sponsor”) and ________ (“Quintiles”) and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________, (the “Master Agreement”), which is incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: This Work Order ("Work Order") is between ________ ("Sponsor") and ________ ("Quintiles") and, together with the Master Services Agreement dated ________ (the "Master Agreement") and all attachments and exhibits hereto, constitutes the complete agreement of the parties for the services described herein, all of which are incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes that the Work Order is "subject to" the Master Agreement but fails to state expressly what governs in the event of a conflict between the two documents. This ambiguity exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to the risk that a counterparty could argue that Work Order-level terms—potentially introduced unilaterally or without Sunesis's full negotiation—override the protective provisions Sunesis secured in the Master Agreement, including indemnification, intellectual property ownership, and liability limitations. Without an explicit conflict-resolution rule, any dispute as to which document controls would be resolved through litigation or adversarial interpretation, creating material legal and financial uncertainty for Sunesis. Making the Master Agreement expressly controlling in the event of conflict preserves the benefit of Sunesis's negotiated protections across all Work Orders issued under it.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Work Order. This document constitutes a "Work Order" under the Master Agreement, and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement, which shall govern and control to the extent of any conflict with this Work Order.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause defers all payment terms and obligations entirely to the attachments without establishing any baseline rule governing expenses — specifically whether expenses are included within the fees or are separately reimbursable, and whether Sunesis Pharmaceuticals must pre-approve them before they are incurred. Without this guardrail on the face of the clause, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals is exposed to open-ended cost liability if the attachments are silent or ambiguous on expense treatment, as a counterparty could assert a right to pass through unrestricted out-of-pocket costs. The practical commercial risk to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals is an inability to control or contest expense charges that were never affirmatively authorized, with no approval mechanism to invoke as a defense.

suggestions.suggested_fix: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses. Any expenses or costs that are not expressly included within the fees set forth in the applicable attachment shall only be reimbursable to the extent pre-approved in writing by Sunesis Pharmaceuticals prior to being incurred.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment terms whatsoever — it is purely an index of attachments, with no provision governing how fees are calculated, when invoices are issued, when payment is due, whether fees may be increased, or what happens in the event of a disputed or late-paid invoice. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, this creates material financial exposure: without a contractually embedded payment framework, the counterparty could assert broad discretion over fee structures and billing cadence, and Sunesis would have no contractual basis to withhold a disputed amount, challenge a fee increase, or resist late-payment penalties. The absence of a dispute mechanism is particularly prejudicial to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, as it may be deemed in default simply for contesting a defective invoice.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Fees shall be calculated as set forth in Attachment 2 and shall not be increased without the prior written consent of Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears and are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Sunesis Pharmaceuticals may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and disputed amounts shall be withheld pending resolution without constituting a payment default. Undisputed amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause, as drafted, exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to significant operational and financial risk because it does not require each Work Order to specify scope, deliverables, timeline, or the basis on which fees are priced, leaving the fundamental commercial terms of each engagement undefined and potentially unenforceable. The clause also fails to require execution by both parties before a Work Order becomes binding, and it contains no change control mechanism, meaning a counterparty could assert scope or cost changes without Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's written consent. Finally, while the clause addresses Master Agreement survivability, it is silent on conflict of terms, leaving open which document controls in the event of inconsistency—a gap that could be exploited against Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's interests in a dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause gives Quintiles unfettered discretion to engage non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants by simply listing them, with no requirement that Sunesis Pharmaceuticals approve, consent to, or object to those parties—and no mechanism to control the addition of new or replacement subcontractors during performance. Critically, while the clause expressly binds Quintiles' affiliates to all terms of the Master Agreement and Work Order, it is entirely silent on whether non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants are subject to equivalent obligations, including confidentiality, data protection, and security—obligations of particular sensitivity given the pharmaceutical context in which proprietary compound data and clinical information are involved. This gap exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to uncontrolled disclosure of its confidential information and regulatory data to third parties over whom it has no contractual privity and against whom it has no direct remedy. Quintiles' primary liability for subcontractor performance is also not stated, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals without a clear avenue of recourse for breaches originating downstream.

Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:

suggestions.reason: The paragraph, as drafted, contains only a bracketed placeholder with no operative language establishing that Quintiles remains responsible for the acts, omissions, or performance failures of any subcontractors or consultants it engages. Without an express responsibility provision, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals is exposed to a significant accountability gap: if a subcontractor causes harm, delays, or regulatory non-compliance in connection with the Services, Quintiles could disclaim direct liability by pointing to the independent conduct of a third party not in privity with Sunesis. This risk is particularly acute in a pharmaceutical services context where subcontractor failures can have material operational, regulatory, and safety consequences for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals.
